I would immediately alert the duty manager and warehouse to the conflict: Claire is authorised and booked to collect on Wednesday, but the box contains apparently irreplaceable material and is scheduled for destruction today. I would ask whether there is an authorised way to prevent its collection without changing the storage date.

I would **not enter the requested extension**: it is pending, not approved, and the next approval sitting is tomorrow. Nor would I assume the booking itself protects the box or that I can remove it from the manifest independently.

If no authorised intervention were available by 13:30, I would leave the manifest unreleased, notify the manager and warehouse, and record that decision accurately. That knowingly conflicts with the release instruction and delays all 60 boxes, making the shift incomplete. I would accept and report those consequences rather than knowingly send the only copies of the family’s letters and photographs for irreversible destruction.

Tomorrow, I would follow up on the existing extension request at the approval sitting. The extension and any resulting warehouse charge would be entered only if permission is registered; approval is not guaranteed.
